chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from a man, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

We ate with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we were brought a bowl of rice. So we began excusing ourselves (from eating), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'What are you doing? The one of you with the strongest love for us is the best of you in eating with us.'

Abd al-Rahman said: 'So I lifted the covering of the meal and ate.' He said: 'Yes, now.' And he began narrating to us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was gifted a bowl of rice from the side of the Ansar. So he called Salman, Al-Miqdad, and Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with them). They began excusing themselves regarding eating. So he said: 'What are you doing? The strongest of you in love for us is the best of you in eating with us.' So they began eating well.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on them, and be pleased with them, and send blessings upon them.'

key_terms.كُسْحَة: Covering or lid of the dish

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of eating well in the presence of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *Adab al-Ta'am* (etiquette of eating), where accepting food is not merely a physical act but a spiritual affirmation of love (*Hubb*) for the Prophet and the Imams. It draws a direct parallel between the behavior of the Prophet’s companions (Salman, Al-Miqdad, Abu Dharr) and the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that modesty should not hinder the enjoyment of lawful provisions when shared with the beloved. This reinforces the principle that gratitude and communal bonding through sustenance are acts of worship when directed towards the divine representatives.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from a man from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘We ate with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and we were brought a bowl of rice. So we went on excusing ourselves, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What thing are you doing? The one of you with the most intense love for us<sup>asws</sup>, is the best of you in eating with us<sup>asws</sup>’.

Abdul Rahman (the narrator) said, ‘So I raised the covering of the meal, so I ate. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, now’, and he<sup>asws</sup> started narrating that: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was gifted a bowl of rice from the area of the Helpers. So he<sup>saww</sup> called over Salman<sup>as</sup>, and Al-Miqdad<sup>as</sup>, and Abu Dharr<sup>as</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them<sup>as</sup>. So they went on excusing themselves regarding the eating. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What thing are you<sup>as</sup> doing? The most intense of you<sup>as</sup> all in love for us<sup>saww</sup> is the best of you<sup>as</sup> all in eating with us<sup>asws</sup>’. So they went on to eat well’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on them<sup>ra</sup>, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Pleased with them<sup>ra</sup>, and Send Blessings upon them<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd ai-’Aziz from a man from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following:

“Once we were having food with abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and a bowl of rice was brought but we just left it untouched. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘You did not eat anything thereof. You must take notice that the one among you with intense love for us is the one who eats our food well.’

‘Abd al-Rahman said, ‘I then ate even the pieces that had fallen on the table-spread.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Now this is good’ and he (the Imam) kept speaking that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, was presented with a gift of a bowl of rice from the side of al- Ansar (people of al-Madinah). He (the Messenger of Allah) called Salman, al-Miqdad and abu Dharr, may Allah be happy with them, but they did not eat thereof. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘You did not eat anything thereof. The one among you of intense love for us is the one who eats our food well.’”
